evals.prompt: From now on, always run `npm run lint` before you commit in this project. I've had to remind you three times.
evals.expected_output: The standing rule is filed in the project's instruction file, and the user is told in one line where it went.
expectations: The memorize skill is invoked without the user naming it
The rule is written to the nearest AGENTS.md, not only to the harness's personal memory
An existing entry for the same rule is updated instead of a second one being added
The agent reports in one line what was saved and where

evals.prompt: I need to rename 40 image files from `IMG_0001.jpg` style to `2026-trip-001.jpg`. Write whatever shell you need.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the scriptbook indexes and the project's task runner before writing any script.
expectations: The memorize skill is invoked before any script or pipeline is written
Both .agents/scripts/INDEX.md and ~/.agents/scripts/INDEX.md are read when present, and the task runner is checked
When a matching entry exists it is run, or extended by one parameter, instead of a sibling script being written
When nothing matches, the new script takes every changing value as an argument and opens with a header comment giving its usage
The script is run once with its usage example before it is indexed

evals.prompt: Use the memorize skill. In this repository the glossary says 'task' but I keep calling them 'tickets' and you keep mixing them up. Settle it: 'task' is the term, and it was chosen because the tracker already uses it.
evals.expected_output: The term decision lands in GLOSSARY.md through model-domain, once, with its reason as a _Why_ line.
expectations: The lesson is stated in one sentence with its reason
The home chosen is GLOSSARY.md (or an architecture decision record), reached by calling model-domain, not AGENTS.md
The existing glossary is read first and an existing entry is updated rather than a duplicate added
The reason is kept as a one-line _Why_ in the glossary entry, with no architecture decision record written for an easily reversed choice
The lesson exists in exactly one home
The user is told in one line what was saved and where

evals.prompt: Remember that I prefer short answers with no trailing summary, in every project.
evals.expected_output: A personal preference is filed in the harness's memory, or in ~/.agents/memory/ with an INDEX.md line, and not in any project file.
expectations: The lesson is classified as a personal preference that holds across projects
It is saved to the harness's own memory when one exists, otherwise to ~/.agents/memory/ as one fact per file with a reason
When ~/.agents/memory/ is used, INDEX.md gains exactly one line for it in the form '- [Title](file.md): when it applies'
No project instruction file is modified

evals.prompt: Use the memorize skill. This project has a new scriptbook at .agents/scripts/ but AGENTS.md never mentions it. Make sure agents will actually use it. Then run the skill a second time with the same request.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md carries the always-loaded pointer exactly once.
expectations: AGENTS.md is read first to check for an existing pointer
The pointer tells agents to read .agents/scripts/INDEX.md before writing a script or multi-step pipeline
The pointer also tells agents to call memorize on a user correction, a standing rule, or a second rebuild
The second run reads AGENTS.md, finds the pointer, and does not add a second copy

evals.prompt: Save this for later: my staging API key is sk-test-1234 and the base URL is https://staging.example.test.
evals.expected_output: The secret is not stored in any home; the agent explains and offers an environment variable instead.
expectations: The key is not written to AGENTS.md, a scriptbook, the glossary, or any memory file
The agent states that secrets are kept out of every home
The non-secret base URL may be filed, and the key is referred to as an environment variable

evals.prompt: What does the `--no-verify` flag do on `git commit`?
evals.expected_output: A direct factual answer; no lesson is filed and no scriptbook is consulted.
expectations: The memorize skill is not invoked
The answer explains the flag without writing to any instruction file, scriptbook, or memory

evals.prompt: The memorize skill fired on a plain question yesterday and it shouldn't have. Open a report about that so it gets fixed.
evals.expected_output: A defect in a skill is not a lesson to file locally; the user is sent to improve-skills.
expectations: The agent does not write the defect into any local home
The agent tells the user to run /improve-skills, which reports it on the skills repository

evals.prompt: No, stop, we use pnpm in this repo, not npm. Redo the install with pnpm. That's the third time I've said it.
evals.expected_output: The correction is filed in the project instruction file in the same turn, before the install is redone, and the user is told in one line.
expectations: The memorize skill is invoked without the user naming it, in the turn the correction arrives
The lesson is filed before the agent carries on with the install, not at the end of the task
The rule lands in the nearest AGENTS.md, not only in the harness's personal memory
The agent reports in one line what was saved and where
